questions.question: Which of the following cities is located in a rain-shadow region in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pune**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pune** is located on the **leeward side** of the Western Ghats, which causes it to experience a **rain-shadow region.**
 
• A rain-shadow region occurs when **mountains obstruct moist winds**, leading to heavy rainfall on the windward side and **dry conditions** on the leeward side.
 
• The Western Ghats block the **southwest monsoon winds**, preventing much of the rain from reaching Pune.
 
• Pune receives an average annual rainfall of approximately **700 mm**, which is relatively low compared to areas on the windward side of the Western Ghats.
 
• This geographical feature makes Pune's climate **semi-arid**, with hot summers and moderate winters.
 
• Despite being in a rain-shadow region, Pune is a major city in **Maharashtra** known for its **educational institutions, IT industry, and cultural heritage.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shillong**__

 __
 
• **Shillong** is located in Meghalaya, which is part of the **northeastern region of India.**
 
• It is situated on the **windward side** of the Khasi Hills, which causes it to receive **heavy rainfall during the monsoon season.**
 
• The nearby **Cherrapunji and Mawsynram** regions are among the **wettest places on Earth.**
 
 
 
• **Cochin**__
 __
 
• **Cochin (Kochi)** is located in the state of **Kerala**, on the **windward side** of the Western Ghats.
 
• It receives abundant rainfall due to the **southwest monsoon winds.**
 
• The city is known for its **backwaters, port, and spice trade.**
 
 
 
• **Goa**__
 
 
• **Goa** is situated on the western coast of India, facing the **Arabian Sea.**
 
• It receives significant rainfall during the **southwest monsoon season.**
 
• Goa is famous for its **beaches, tourism, and Portuguese heritage.**

questions.question: Which Indian state receives rainfall from both, the Southwest and Northeast monsoons?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu** is unique among Indian states as it receives rainfall from both the **Southwest Monsoon** and the **Northeast Monsoon**.
 
• The state receives the majority of its rainfall during the **Northeast Monsoon** (October to December), which is also known as the **Retreating Monsoon**.
 
• During the **Southwest Monsoon** (June to September), Tamil Nadu receives rainfall primarily in the western parts of the state due to the **Western Ghats** acting as an orographic barrier.
 
• The **Northeast Monsoon** is vital for Tamil Nadu as it contributes to about **48% of the total annual rainfall** in the state.
 
• The geographical location of Tamil Nadu, being adjacent to the **Bay of Bengal**, plays a crucial role in attracting cyclonic systems and heavy rainfall during the Northeast Monsoon.
 
• Major cities like **Chennai** and the **Cauvery Delta region** rely heavily on the Northeast Monsoon for their water requirements.
 
• This dual monsoon pattern is critical for **agriculture, water resources, and livelihood** in Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bihar**__

 __
 
• **Bihar** receives most of its rainfall during the **Southwest Monsoon** (June to September).
 
• The state does not benefit significantly from the **Northeast Monsoon**, as its geographical location lies far from the influence of retreating monsoon winds.
 
• **Kosi River**, often termed the “Sorrow of Bihar,” causes severe flooding during the monsoon season.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**__
 __
 
• **Maharashtra** receives rainfall predominantly during the **Southwest Monsoon** (June to September).
 
• The state is home to the **Western Ghats**, which experience heavy orographic rainfall during this period.
 
• Regions such as **Konkan** and **Western Maharashtra** are particularly known for their heavy monsoon rains.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**__
 
 
• **Gujarat** receives most of its rainfall from the **Southwest Monsoon**, particularly during the months of June to September.
 
• The state is located in a semi-arid region, and the rainfall is unevenly distributed, with **Saurashtra** receiving less precipitation compared to other parts.
 
• The **Narmada River** and projects like the **Sardar Sarovar Dam** play a significant role in water management for the state.

questions.question: How are the Himalayan ranges oriented in Arunachal Pradesh
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Southwest to Northwest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayan ranges** in Arunachal Pradesh are oriented in the **Southwest to Northwest direction.**
 
• This region is characterized by the **Eastern Himalayas**, which include some of the most rugged and remote terrains in India.
 
• The orientation of the ranges is influenced by the ** and the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate.**
 
• In Arunachal Pradesh, the Himalayas consist of ranges such as the **Siang, Mishmi, and Patkai Hills**, which follow this southwest-to-northwest alignment.
 
• The natural orientation plays a crucial role in defining the **climatic conditions**, **river systems**, and **vegetation** of the region.
 
• It is also important for the **local biodiversity**, as the Eastern Himalayas are known for their rich flora and fauna.
 
• The region is part of the **Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot**, which is globally recognized for its ecological significance.
 
• Key rivers such as the **Brahmaputra** and its tributaries originate or pass through these ranges, further highlighting their geographical importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **North to South Orientation**__

 __
 
• In the context of Indian geography, the **North to South orientation** is not characteristic of the Himalayan ranges but can be seen in smaller regional features or mountain ranges.
 
• Examples include certain ranges of the Western Ghats or mountain systems with localized alignments.
 
 
 
• **Northwest to Southeast Orientation**__
 __
 
• This orientation is typical for the **general alignment of the Himalayas** in their western parts.
 
• Ranges such as the **Pir Panjal** and parts of the **Shivalik Hills** follow this alignment.
 
• However, this does not apply to the Himalayan ranges in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **East to West Orientation**__
 
 
• The East to West orientation is generally seen in the **Trans-Himalayan ranges** and certain geographical features outside the Indian subcontinent.
 
• In India, this alignment is rare for the Himalayas and is more characteristic of other mountain systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a physiographic subdivision of the Northern Plains of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Vindhyan Plateau**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vindhyan Plateau** is not a part of the physiographic subdivisions of the Northern Plains of India.
 
• The Northern Plains are primarily divided into regions based on the deposition of alluvial soil brought by rivers such as the **Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus**.
 
• The Vindhyan Plateau is part of the **Peninsular Plateau**, which is a distinct physiographic region of India.
 
• It is characterized by **rugged terrain, hard rocks, and plateaus**, unlike the fertile alluvial plains of the Northern Plains.
 
• The Vindhyan Plateau lies in central India and is bounded by the **Vindhya mountain range**.
 
• This region is composed predominantly of **sedimentary rocks**, and it does not feature the characteristics associated with the Northern Plains.
 
• The physiographic divisions of the Northern Plains include **Bhangar, Khadar, Tarai Tract, and floodplains**, all of which are alluvial regions formed by river systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhangar**__

 __
 
• **Bhangar** refers to the older alluvium deposits found in the Northern Plains of India.
 
• It is characterized by a slightly elevated terrain compared to the **Khadar** regions.
 
• Bhangar soils are less fertile as they contain **calcareous deposits** called 'Kankar'.
 
 
 
• **Tarai Tract**__
 __
 
• The **Tarai Tract** is a marshy region located at the foothills of the Himalayas.
 
• This region is formed due to the percolation of rivers as they enter the plains, leading to waterlogged soil.
 
• The Tarai is known for its rich **biodiversity** and is home to several national parks, such as **Jim Corbett National Park**.
 
 
 
• **Khadar**__
 
 
• **Khadar** refers to the newer alluvium deposits found in the floodplains of rivers in the Northern Plains.
 
• It is highly fertile due to the continuous deposition of fresh alluvium during floods.
 
• Khadar regions are preferred for **agricultural activities**.

questions.question: Anaimudi, the highest peak in South India, is located at the tri-junction of which three hill ranges?

options.text: Nilgiri Hills, Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats
Rajmahal Hills, Garo Hills, Khasi Hills
Annamalai Range, Cardamom Hills, Palani Hills
Mahadeo Hills, Maikala Range, Rajpipla Hills

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Annamalai Range, Cardamom Hills, Palani Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anaimudi** is the **highest peak in South India**, with an elevation of **2,695 meters (8,842 feet)** above sea level.
 
• It is located in the **Western Ghats** mountain range in the state of **Kerala**, India.
 
• The peak lies at the **tri-junction of three major hill ranges**: **Annamalai Range**, **Cardamom Hills**, and **Palani Hills**.
 
• The name "Anaimudi" translates to "**Elephant's Forehead**" in Tamil and Malayalam, reflecting the shape of the peak.
 
• The region surrounding Anaimudi is home to the **Eravikulam National Park**, which is known for its rich biodiversity, including the **Nilgiri Tahr**, an endangered species of mountain goat.
 
• Anaimudi is a significant destination for **trekking enthusiasts** and offers breathtaking views of the lush greenery and tea plantations of the Western Ghats.
 
• The peak is also an important part of the **UNESCO World Heritage-listed Western Ghats**, recognized for its ecological and cultural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nilgiri Hills, Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats**__

 __
 
• The **Nilgiri Hills** are part of the **Western Ghats**, located in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. However, Anaimudi is not situated at the tri-junction of these ranges.
 
• The **Eastern Ghats** are a discontinuous range of mountains along the eastern coast of India, distinct from the Western Ghats.
 
 
 
• **Rajmahal Hills, Garo Hills, Khasi Hills**__
 __
 
• The **Rajmahal Hills** are located in Jharkhand, and the **Garo Hills** and **Khasi Hills** are in Meghalaya in northeastern India.
 
• These hills are not related to the location of Anaimudi or the Western Ghats.
 
 
 
• **Mahadeo Hills, Maikala Range, Rajpipla Hills**__
 
 
• The **Mahadeo Hills** are located in Madhya Pradesh, while the **Maikala Range** is in Chhattisgarh, and the **Rajpipla Hills** are in Gujarat.
 
• These ranges are not part of the Western Ghats or associated with Anaimudi.

questions.question: Which of the following ports is located in West Coastal Plain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mangalore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mangalore Port** is located in the state of Karnataka along the **West Coastal Plain** of India.
 
• It is a major port situated on the Arabian Sea, primarily used for the export of iron ore, coffee, spices, and other goods.
 
• The port is officially known as **New Mangalore Port** and is one of the 12 major ports in India.
 
• Mangalore's strategic location on the west coast makes it a crucial hub for maritime trade and economic activities in the region.
 
• It plays a key role in connecting Karnataka and its industries to global markets, particularly through its well-developed infrastructure and facilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **West Coastal Plain of India**

 
 
• It lies between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, extending from Gujarat in the north to Kerala in the south.
 
• The plain is divided into three sections: the Konkan Coast (Maharashtra-Goa), the Kanara Coast (Karnataka), and the Malabar Coast (Kerala).
 
• It is known for its fertile soil, lush greenery, and a significant number of ports facilitating maritime trade.
 
 
 
• **Other Major Ports on the West Coast**
 
 
• Mumbai Port and Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Maharashtra)
 
• Kandla Port (Gujarat)
 
• Cochin Port (Kerala)
 
 
 
• **Role of Ports in Indian Economy**
 
 
• Ports play a critical role in India's international trade, handling approximately 95% of the country's trade volume by weight.
 
• The west coast ports are particularly significant due to their proximity to Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.
 
 
 
• **Arabian Sea**
 
 
• The Arabian Sea is a part of the northern Indian Ocean, bordered by India, Pakistan, and Iran.
 
• It is a key route for international maritime trade, connecting the Indian subcontinent to global markets.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension measured by the Gender Inequality Index (GII)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Access to clean drinking water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gender Inequality Index (GII) is a composite index measuring disparities in achievements between men and women in three dimensions: reproductive health, empowerment, and labor market participation.
 
• **Reproductive health** is measured by maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rates.
 
• **Empowerment** is measured by the proportion of parliamentary seats held by women and the proportion of women and men aged 25 years and older with at least some secondary education.
 
• **Labor market participation** is assessed by the labor force participation rate of women compared to men.
 
• Access to clean drinking water is not considered a dimension in the Gender Inequality Index, as GII focuses on gender-specific inequalities rather than general living conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gender Inequality Index (GII):**

 
 
• Introduced by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in its 2010 Human Development Report.
 
• It highlights areas where women are disadvantaged compared to men.
 
• The GII ranges from 0 (no inequality) to 1 (complete inequality).
 
 
 
• **Reproductive Health Indicators:**
 
 
• Maternal mortality ratio: The number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.
 
• Adolescent birth rate: The number of births per 1,000 women aged 15-19 years.
 
 
 
• **Empowerment Indicators:**
 
 
• Proportion of parliamentary seats held by women: Reflects political representation and decision-making power.
 
• Educational attainment: Tracks the percentage of women and men with at least some secondary education.
 
 
 
• **Labor Force Participation:**
 
 
• Compares the percentage of women and men actively engaged in the labor market.
 
• It includes both employed individuals and those actively seeking employment.

questions.question: The Palk Strait separates India from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Palk Strait **is a narrow stretch of water separating **India and Sri Lanka**.
 
• It **connects the Bay of Bengal **in the northeast **with the Gulf of Mannar **in the southwest.
 
• On the Indian side, the Palk Strait borders the state of Tamil Nadu, while on the Sri Lankan side, it borders the Northern Province.
 
• Adam's Bridge (also known as Ram Setu), a chain of limestone shoals, lies within the Palk Strait and historically connected India to Sri Lanka.
 
• The Palk Strait is named after Robert Palk, a British governor of Madras during the 18th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geography of the Palk Strait:**

 
 
• The strait is approximately 40 to 85 miles (64 to 137 km) wide.
 
• It is relatively shallow, making navigation challenging for large ships.
 
 
 
• **Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu):**
 
 
• A chain of natural limestone shoals, believed to have formed naturally.
 
• It holds mythological significance in the Indian epic Ramayana as the bridge built by Lord Rama’s army to reach Lanka.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• The strait supports fishing and trade activities between India and Sri Lanka.
 
• It holds strategic importance for maritime routes in the Indian Ocean region.
 
 
 
• **Marine Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The Palk Strait is home to diverse marine life, including fish, crustaceans, and seaweed.
 
• Efforts are being made to preserve its unique ecosystem due to overfishing and habitat destruction.

questions.question: What is the region lying to the north of the Narmada River called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Highlands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The region lying to the north of the Narmada River is referred to as the **Central Highlands**.
 
• The Central Highlands are bounded by the **Aravalli Hills in the northwest** and the Vindhyan Range to the south.
 
• This region is part of the **northern extension of the Peninsular Plateau of India**.
 
• The Central Highlands include the **Malwa Plateau** and parts of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The rivers in this region primarily flow from the south to the north due to the **slope of the plateau**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada River**

 
 
• The Narmada River is considered the **traditional boundary** separating North and South India.
 
• It flows westward, unlike most other rivers in India, which flow eastward.
 
• The Narmada originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in Madhya Pradesh and drains into the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• **Vindhyan Range**
 
 
• The Vindhyan Range acts as a **southern boundary for the Central Highlands**.
 
• It is one of the oldest mountain ranges in India, predominantly made of sandstone.
 
• It plays a significant role in separating the Indo-Gangetic Plains from the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Range**
 
 
• The Aravalli Range, located in northwestern India, is one of the **oldest fold mountains in the world**.
 
• It forms the **northwestern boundary of the Central Highlands**.
 
• The range is known for its rich mineral deposits and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Peninsular Plateau**
 
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is the **oldest landmass** of India, formed during the Precambrian era.
 
• It is divided into two major parts: the **Central Highlands** and the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• This plateau is rich in natural resources, including minerals, forests, and fertile soil.

questions.question: The subtropical jet stream plays a critical role in the withdrawal of the monsoon by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inducing subsidence over land**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The subtropical jet stream shifts southward during the monsoon withdrawal phase, causing a **high-pressure system to develop over land**.
 
• This high-pressure system leads to **subsidence (downward movement of air)**, which suppresses convection and reduces rainfall.
 
• Subsidence over land promotes the **replacement of moist monsoonal winds with dry winds**, marking the retreat of the monsoon.
 
• The subtropical jet stream plays a pivotal role by inducing large-scale atmospheric stability, halting further moisture advection from the oceans.
 
• As a result, the **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)** shifts southward, coinciding with the monsoon withdrawal process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subtropical Jet Stream:**

 
 
• A high-altitude, fast-moving air current located around 30° latitude in both hemispheres.
 
• It plays a critical role in influencing weather patterns, including the onset and withdrawal of monsoons.
 
 
 
• **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ):**
 
 
• A low-pressure zone near the equator where trade winds converge, leading to upward motion and cloud formation.
 
• The ITCZ shifts seasonally, influencing monsoon dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Subsidence:**
 
 
• The downward movement of air in the atmosphere, which suppresses cloud formation and precipitation.
 
• Often associated with the presence of high-pressure systems.
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Withdrawal:**
 
 
• The retreat of monsoonal winds marked by decreasing rainfall and the establishment of dry continental air over the region.
 
• Typically begins in northwest India and progresses southeastward.
 
 
 
• **Cold Air Advection:**
 
 
• The horizontal movement of cooler air into a region, often associated with the strengthening of high-pressure systems.
 
• While cold air advection plays a role in weather changes, it is not directly responsible for monsoon withdrawal.

questions.question: During which phase and year was a steady population growth rate observed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phase II: 1921-1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The period from **1921 to 1951** is classified as Phase II in India's demographic history.
 
• During this phase, India saw a steady growth in its population due to improvements in **healthcare and sanitation**.
 
• This phase marked the beginning of a decline in mortality rates, although **birth rates remained high**.
 
• The steady population growth can be attributed to **better control of epidemics**, availability of vaccines, and improved public health measures.
 
• Phase II is often referred to as the "early expanding stage" in the demographic transition model.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demographic Transition Model (DTM):** It explains the transition of countries from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates through economic and social development.
 
• **Phase I (1891-1921):** Known as the "stagnant stage," India experienced very low population growth due to high mortality rates caused by famines, epidemics, and poor healthcare.
 
• **Phase III (1951-1981):** Characterized by rapid population growth due to a significant decline in death rates while birth rates remained high.
 
• **Phase IV (1981-2011):** Marked by a slowing population growth rate as birth rates began to decline due to family planning and increased literacy.
 
• **Factors Leading to Population Growth:** Economic development, improved medical facilities, access to education, and better hygiene practices are key contributors to population changes over time.

questions.question: 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are important crops of which of the following in states like Assam, West Bengal and Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aus, Aman, and Boro** are three major varieties of paddy grown in India, particularly in the eastern states like Assam, West Bengal, and Odisha.
 
• The cultivation of these varieties depends heavily on the **monsoon and water availability** for irrigation.
 
• **Aman** paddy is sown during the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in winter (November-December).
 
• **Aus** paddy is cultivated during the pre-monsoon season and harvested before the onset of the monsoon.
 
• **Boro** paddy is grown during the dry season (November to May) using irrigation facilities, making it a winter crop.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:** Paddy refers to rice in its raw, unprocessed form, which is grown as a staple food crop in many parts of India.
 
• **Climatic Requirements:** Paddy requires a hot and humid climate, with temperatures ranging between 20°C to 35°C and a minimum of 100 cm of annual rainfall.
 
• **Geographical Importance:** Assam, West Bengal, and Odisha are among the largest producers of paddy in India due to their fertile soil and favorable climatic conditions.
 
• **Economic Significance:** Paddy farming plays a crucial role in the agrarian economy of India, providing livelihood to millions of farmers and contributing significantly to food security.
 
• **Green Revolution Impact:** The introduction of high-yielding rice varieties during the Green Revolution significantly boosted paddy production in India.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers rises in the western slopes of the Aravalli Range near Ajmer, where it is known as the Sagarmati?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Luni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Luni River originates in the western slopes of the **Aravalli Range**, near Ajmer, Rajasthan.
 
• In its initial stages, the river is locally known as the **Sagarmati**.
 
• It is a significant river of the arid region of **Rajasthan**, often referred to as the lifeline of the desert.
 
• The Luni flows through Rajasthan and Gujarat before ending in the marshy lands of the **Rann of Kutch**.
 
• Unlike most rivers, the Luni is a **saline river**, which makes it unique among Indian rivers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aravalli Range:**

 
 
• The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, located in western India.
 
• It stretches across Rajasthan, Haryana, and Gujarat.
 
• Ajmer, where the Luni originates, is situated in the central part of this range.
 
 
 
• **Rivers in Rajasthan:**
 
 
• Rajasthan is known for its arid climate and has several seasonal rivers.
 
• Other prominent rivers in Rajasthan include Chambal, Banas, and Saraswati.
 
 
 
• **Saline Rivers:**
 
 
• The Luni becomes saline as it passes through the desert, due to the high salt content in the soil.
 
• This salinity limits its usability for drinking and irrigation purposes in its lower stretches.
 
 
 
• **Rann of Kutch:**
 
 
• The Rann of Kutch is a large salt marsh located in Gujarat, where the Luni ends.
 
• It is part of the Thar Desert and serves as a unique ecosystem for flora and fauna.

questions.question: In which Indian state are the Kachchh and Kathiawar coasts located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kachchh (Kutch) and Kathiawar coasts are located in the state of **Gujarat**, India.
 
• Kachchh is known for its unique geographical features, including the **Rann of Kutch**, which is a salt marsh.
 
• The Kathiawar Peninsula, located in Gujarat, is bordered by the Arabian Sea and is home to **the Gir National Park**, the last refuge of the Asiatic lions.
 
• These coasts are significant for their **marine biodiversity, salt production, and mangrove ecosystems**.
 
• Both regions are key contributors to Gujarat's economy through industries like salt manufacturing, agriculture, and tourism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kachchh Region:**

 
 
• The Rann of Kutch is divided into two parts—**Great Rann** and **Little Rann**.
 
• The area experiences extreme climate conditions, with hot summers and cold winters.
 
• The region is famous for its annual festival, the **Rann Utsav**, which showcases local art, culture, and heritage.
 
 
 
• **Kathiawar Peninsula:**
 
 
• It is bounded by the Arabian Sea to the west and south, the Gulf of Kutch to the northwest, and the Gulf of Khambhat to the southeast.
 
• It is rich in historical sites, including the ancient city of **Dwarka**, a significant pilgrimage site in Hindu mythology.
 
• The region is home to the Gir Forest, which is the only natural habitat of the **Asiatic lion**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• Gujarat is one of the largest producers of salt in India, with the Kutch region being a major contributor.
 
• The coastal areas support industries such as **fishing, shipbuilding, and petrochemicals**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Significance:**
 
 
• The coastal areas are home to extensive **mangrove forests**, which act as natural barriers against coastal erosion.
 
• These regions are part of the **Global Biodiversity Hotspots** and are crucial for migratory birds and marine species.

questions.question: _____ recorded the highest population density in 2011, as per the 2011 Census of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North East Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **2011 Census of India**, North East Delhi recorded the **highest population density** in the country.
 
• North East Delhi had a population density of **37,346 persons per square kilometer**, making it the most densely populated district in India.
 
• Population density is calculated as the number of persons per square kilometer of land area.
 
• North East Delhi is part of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi, which is itself one of the most urbanized and densely populated regions in India.
 
• The high population density in this region is attributed to urbanization, migration, and the concentration of residential settlements in limited geographic space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:**

 
 
• Population density is a key demographic indicator that reflects the number of people living in a unit area of land.
 
• It is calculated using the formula: **Population Density = Total Population / Land Area**.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census of India:**
 
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of India and provided comprehensive data on population demographics, density, literacy, and other parameters.
 
• It recorded India's population at **1.21 billion**, with a growth rate of 17.7% compared to 2001.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization in Delhi:**
 
 
• Delhi’s rapid urbanization has resulted in high population density, particularly in areas like North East Delhi.
 
• Migrants from different states move to Delhi for job opportunities, education, and improved living standards, contributing to its dense population.
 
 
 
• **Other High-Density Districts:**
 
 
• After North East Delhi, other districts with high population densities include **Central Delhi** and **East Delhi**.
 
• These regions also face challenges such as overcrowding, pressure on infrastructure, and environmental concerns.

questions.question: Which of these agricultural regions is best known for rice-wheat cropping system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-Gangetic Plains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indo-Gangetic Plains are one of the most fertile agricultural regions in India, supporting the rice-wheat cropping system.
 
• This cropping system is practiced in states like Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar due to favorable climate and soil conditions.
 
• Rice is grown during the Kharif season (monsoon) as it requires a significant amount of water, while wheat is cultivated in the Rabi season (winter).
 
• The alluvial soil of the Indo-Gangetic Plains, coupled with abundant water resources from rivers like the Ganga and its tributaries, makes the region ideal for this cropping system.
 
• This system contributes significantly to India's food security, with the region being called the "Granary of India."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif Crops:**

 
 
• These are crops grown during the monsoon season (June to October) and include rice, maize, and millets.
 
• Rice is the most prominent Kharif crop in the Indo-Gangetic Plains due to the high water availability during this period.
 
 
 
• **Rabi Crops:**
 
 
• These are crops grown in the winter season (November to April), such as wheat, barley, and mustard.
 
• Wheat cultivation in the Rabi season complements rice, forming the rice-wheat cropping pattern in the Indo-Gangetic Plains.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Soil:**
 
 
• The Indo-Gangetic Plains are rich in alluvial soil, brought by rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna, and their tributaries.
 
• This soil is highly fertile and suitable for growing a wide variety of crops, including rice and wheat.
 
 
 
• **Food Security in India:**
 
 
• The rice-wheat cropping system in the Indo-Gangetic Plains contributes significantly to India's food grain production.
 
• This region plays a critical role in ensuring food security for the country, feeding millions of people.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution:**
 
 
• The Indo-Gangetic Plains were a major beneficiary of the Green Revolution in the 1960s-70s, which introduced high-yield variety seeds and improved irrigation methods.
 
• This led to a significant increase in the productivity of rice and wheat in the region.

questions.question: Which canal project plays a major role in irrigation in the Thar Desert?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indira Gandhi Canal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Indira Gandhi Canal** is one of the largest canal systems in India, and it plays a vital role in providing water for irrigation in the **Thar Desert** region.
 
• The canal originates at the **Harike Barrage**, located at the confluence of the Sutlej and Beas rivers in Punjab, and flows through Rajasthan.
 
• It was commissioned in **1984** and provides water to the arid regions of **western Rajasthan**, including Jodhpur, Bikaner, and surrounding areas.
 
• The canal irrigates around **19 lakh hectares** of land, transforming barren areas into fertile agricultural lands in the desert.
 
• The project has significantly contributed to the socio-economic development of the region, ensuring food security and better livelihoods for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the **Great Indian Desert**, is the 17th largest desert in the world and covers approximately **200,000 square kilometers**.
 
• It spans the states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, with **Rajasthan** having the largest share.
 
• It is characterized by **extreme arid conditions**, high temperatures, and low rainfall (100-200 mm annually).
 
 
 
• **Harike Barrage:**
 
 
• The Harike Barrage is located in Punjab and serves as the source of the Indira Gandhi Canal.
 
• The barrage helps regulate the water flow from the **Sutlej and Beas rivers** into the canal system.
 
 
 
• **Water Management in Arid Regions:**
 
 
• The Indira Gandhi Canal project demonstrates how **large-scale irrigation systems** can combat desertification and promote agricultural activities in arid regions.
 
• It is an example of utilizing **inter-basin water transfer** to address water scarcity.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The Indira Gandhi Canal has boosted agriculture, created employment opportunities, and improved the quality of life for people in western Rajasthan.
 
• It has facilitated the cultivation of crops such as wheat, mustard, and cotton, which were previously impossible in the desert environment.

questions.question: The Chotanagpur Plateau is drained by which river system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Damodar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Damodar River is the primary river system that drains the **Chotanagpur Plateau**, located in eastern India.
 
• It flows through the states of **Jharkhand and West Bengal**, contributing significantly to the region's hydrology.
 
• The river is often referred to as the **"Sorrow of Bengal"** due to its history of frequent flooding.
 
• Major tributaries of the Damodar River include **Barakar, Konar, and Bokaro**, which originate in the Chotanagpur Plateau.
 
• The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) was established in 1948 to control flooding, provide irrigation, and develop hydroelectric projects along the river.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chotanagpur Plateau:**

 
 
• The plateau spans across Jharkhand, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh and is rich in **mineral resources**, such as coal, iron ore, and mica.
 
• It is divided into three sub-regions: **Ranchi Plateau, Hazaribagh Plateau,** and **Pat Plateau**.
 
• The terrain is characterized by rugged hills, valleys, and escarpments, making it a unique geographical region.
 
 
 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC):**
 
 
• DVC is a multipurpose river valley project established in **1948** for flood control, irrigation, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• It manages the Damodar River basin and operates several dams, such as **Tilaiya, Konar, Maithon,** and **Panchet**.
 
 
 
• **Barakar River:**
 
 
• The Barakar River is the largest tributary of the Damodar River and originates in the Chotanagpur Plateau.
 
• It contributes significantly to the water flow in the Damodar River system.
 
 
 
• **Flood Management:**
 
 
• The Damodar River was infamous for annual floods, which devastated agricultural fields and settlements until the establishment of DVC.
 
• Modern flood management practices have reduced the severity and frequency of flooding in the region.

questions.question: Most of the Thar desert lies within India, spanning the states of _________

options.text: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh
Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Madhya Pradesh
Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Himachal Pradesh

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is predominantly located in the northwestern region of India.
 
• It spans across the Indian states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, making it a significant geographical feature in these areas.
 
• The desert covers approximately 77,000 square miles (200,000 square kilometers), with Rajasthan accounting for the majority of its land area.
 
• It is characterized by arid conditions, sand dunes, sparse vegetation, and extreme temperatures, making it one of the most inhospitable regions in India.
 
• The Thar Desert also extends into Pakistan, but the majority of its area lies within Indian territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate of the Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert experiences an arid climate with very low rainfall, typically less than 200mm annually.
 
• Temperatures can soar above 50°C in the summer and drop below freezing in the winter.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Significance:**
 
 
• The desert hosts unique flora and fauna adapted to its harsh conditions, including desert foxes, camels, and khejri trees.
 
• The Desert National Park located in Rajasthan is a protected area that showcases the biodiversity of the region.
 
 
 
• **Human Settlement:**
 
 
• The Thar Desert is one of the world's most densely populated deserts, with villages scattered across its landscape.
 
• Traditional occupations in the region include camel breeding, agriculture (using irrigation), and handicrafts.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features:**
 
 
• Sand dunes, salt pans, and rocky outcrops are prominent features of the Thar Desert's terrain.
 
• The Luni River is the only major river flowing through the desert region.

questions.question: According to the 2011 Census, which island in Lakshadweep has the smallest population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census, **Bitra** is the smallest inhabited island in the Lakshadweep archipelago in terms of population.
 
• The population of Bitra was recorded as **only 271 people**, making it the least populous among all islands in Lakshadweep.
 
• Bitra is geographically the smallest inhabited island, covering an area of approximately **0.105 square kilometers**.
 
• The island serves primarily as a fishing village, with a small number of families residing there.
 
• The nearest inhabited island to Bitra is **Chetlat**, which is located approximately 50 kilometers away.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Lakshadweep:**

 
 
• It is a union territory of India consisting of **36 islands**, of which only 10 are inhabited.
 
• Lakshadweep is located in the **Arabian Sea**, about 200-440 km off the southwestern coast of India.
 
• The islands are known for their **coral atolls, reefs, and lagoons**, which make them ecologically and economically significant.
 
 
 
• **Census in India:**
 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years, with the latest available data from the **2011 Census**.
 
• It provides vital information on population, demographics, literacy, and socioeconomic parameters.
 
 
 
• **Bitra's Unique Demographics:**
 
 
• Bitra has the **highest sex ratio** among all islands in Lakshadweep, with 1,384 females per 1,000 males as per the 2011 Census.
 
• The small population size makes it a closely-knit community.
 
 
 
• **Economic Activities in Lakshadweep:**
 
 
• The primary livelihood of the inhabitants is **fishing**, followed by coconut cultivation.
 
• The region also promotes sustainable tourism to preserve its fragile ecosystem.

questions.question: Which of the following urban areas is identified as Million Plus Urban Agglomerations Cities as per Census of India 2001?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census of India 2001, Million Plus Urban Agglomerations Cities are those urban areas with a population exceeding one million.
 
• Lucknow, the capital city of Uttar Pradesh, was identified as one of the Million Plus Urban Agglomerations Cities in the Census 2001.
 
• Lucknow's population crossed the one million mark during the 2001 census, making it eligible for this classification.
 
• Other notable cities like Chandigarh also fall under this category, but Lucknow specifically satisfies the criteria for the given question.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Agglomeration:**

 
 
• An Urban Agglomeration (UA) consists of a core city and its adjoining areas forming a continuous urban spread.
 
• It includes the main city, towns, and outgrowths (like railway colonies, university campuses, etc.) linked to the urban core.
 
 
 
• **Million Plus Cities:**

• Such cities are key focus areas for infrastructure development under schemes like Smart Cities Mission.
 
 
 
• **Census of India:**

questions.question: What is another name for the Great Himalayan range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inner Himalayas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Inner Himalayas, also referred to as the Great Himalayan Range, are the **highest mountain range in the Himalayas**.
 
• This range contains some of the world's tallest peaks, including **Mount Everest (8,849m)**, Kanchenjunga (8,586m), and Nanga Parbat (8,126m).
 
• The Great Himalayan range serves as a natural boundary between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• It spans across five countries: **India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, and Pakistan**, making it a significant geographical feature of South Asia.
 
• It is characterized by **perpetual snow cover, glaciers, and alpine vegetation**, contributing to its ecological and hydrological significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shiwalik Range**

 
 
• The Shiwalik Range, also known as the Outer Himalayas, is the **lowest and southernmost range of the Himalayas**.
 
• It is composed of unconsolidated sediments like sandstone and conglomerates, making it prone to erosion.
 
• The elevation of the Shiwalik Range typically varies from **600 to 1,200 meters above sea level**.
 
• It forms a transition zone between the plains and the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Central Axial Range**
 
 
• This term is not commonly used to describe the Great Himalayan range but may refer to the central spine of the Himalayan region.
 
• It generally includes peaks from the Inner Himalayas like Everest and Kanchenjunga.
 
 
 
• **Northeastern Hills**
 
 
• The Northeastern Hills are a distinct geographical region in India, located in the northeastern states such as Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, and Meghalaya.
 
• They are not part of the Great Himalayan Range but are a separate geological formation.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance of the Inner Himalayas**
 
 
• The Inner Himalayas act as a **source of perennial rivers** such as the Ganges, Indus, and Brahmaputra, vital for agriculture and human settlements.
 
• The range supports a variety of flora and fauna, including endangered species like the snow leopard and red panda.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **regulating climate** and maintaining biodiversity in the region.

questions.question: Which plateau lies between the Aravali and the Vindhya Range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Malwa Plateau is located in the central part of India and lies **between the Aravali and Vindhya ranges**.
 
• It is primarily spread across the states of **Madhya Pradesh** and **Rajasthan**, with some portions extending into Gujarat.
 
• The plateau is characterized by **black soil**, which is highly fertile and suitable for agriculture, particularly for crops like wheat, cotton, and soybean.
 
• This region is also known for its geological significance, being a part of the **Deccan Traps**, which are made up of volcanic basalt rock.
 
• Key rivers such as the **Chambal, Kali Sindh, and Parbati** originate or flow through the Malwa Plateau, enriching the region's agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aravali Range:**

 
 
• One of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, running diagonally across Rajasthan and parts of Haryana and Gujarat.
 
• It acts as a natural barrier, influencing the climate and biodiversity of the region.
 
 
 
• **Vindhya Range:**
 
 
• A mountain range running parallel to the Narmada River, forming the southern boundary of the Malwa Plateau.
 
• It is geologically younger than the Aravali range and influences the northern boundary of the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Traps:**
 
 
• A large igneous province in west-central India, formed due to volcanic activity around 66 million years ago.
 
• The basaltic rock formations contribute to the region's black soil, which is ideal for agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Key Cities:**
 
 
• Important cities located in the Malwa Plateau include **Indore, Ujjain, Ratlam, and Neemuch**.
 
• Ujjain is a major religious and cultural hub, known for the **Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The plateau is rich in mineral resources like limestone and is a hub for cement production.
 
• It also plays a crucial role in agriculture, being one of the most fertile regions in central India.

questions.question: In everyday life, higher population density in cities like Delhi leads to _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**stress on the environment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Higher population density** **in cities increases resource consumption**, leading to a strain on natural resources such as water, air, and land.
 
• Urban areas like Delhi experience elevated levels of air pollution due to increased vehicular emissions and industrial activities.
 
• Overcrowding and rapid urbanization cause improper waste management and disposal, contributing to environmental degradation.
 
• High population density results in deforestation and encroachment on green spaces to accommodate housing and infrastructure needs.
 
• Excessive human activity in densely populated cities disrupts ecological balance, impacting biodiversity and ecosystem services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:**

 
 
• It refers to the number of people living per unit area, typically measured in persons per square kilometer.
 
• High population density can lead to increased demand for housing, transportation, and public services.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Stress:**
 
 
• This term denotes the pressure exerted on environmental systems due to human activities.
 
• Examples include pollution, resource depletion, and habitat destruction.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization:**
 
 
• It is the process by which rural areas transform into urban areas due to migration and infrastructure development.
 
• Unplanned urbanization often leads to environmental challenges like water scarcity and air pollution.
 
 
 
• **Pollution Types:**
 
 
• Air pollution: Caused by vehicle emissions and industrial activities.
 
• Water pollution: Results from untreated sewage and industrial discharge.
 
• Land pollution: Caused by improper waste disposal and deforestation.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Urban Development:**
 
 
• Focuses on creating eco-friendly cities with efficient waste management, green spaces, and renewable energy usage.
 
• Encourages practices like rainwater harvesting and reducing carbon footprints.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers forms the Majuli Island, the world's largest river island?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Majuli Island is located in the state of Assam, India, and is formed by the Brahmaputra River.
 
• The Brahmaputra River flows through Tibet (China), India, and Bangladesh, making it one of the major rivers in South Asia.
 
• Majuli became the world's largest river island and is renowned for its vibrant culture, particularly the neo-Vaishnavite monasteries called "Satras."
 
• The island is surrounded by the Brahmaputra River on the south and the Kherkutia Xuti and Subansiri River on the north.
 
• Majuli Island covers an area of approximately 352 square kilometers and is prone to erosion due to the dynamic nature of the Brahmaputra River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmaputra River**

 
 
• The Brahmaputra originates from the Angsi Glacier in Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo.
 
• It is one of the few rivers in the world that is considered a male river due to its strong currents and dynamic nature.
 
• The Brahmaputra is known for its high sediment load, which contributes to the formation and erosion of islands like Majuli.
 
• It is vital for agriculture, transportation, and water resources in northeastern India.
 
 
 
• **River Islands and Erosion**
 
 
• River islands are formed due to sediment deposition caused by the dynamic flow of rivers.
 
• Majuli faces severe erosion, losing significant land area over time due to changes in the Brahmaputra's course.
 
• Efforts are underway to combat erosion and preserve the cultural heritage of Majuli.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance of Majuli**
 
 
• Majuli is a center for the neo-Vaishnavite tradition initiated by Srimanta Sankardeva in Assam.
 
• It hosts numerous "Satras," which are monasteries that serve as hubs for religious and cultural activities.
 
• The island is also known for its traditional art forms, pottery, and festivals.

questions.question: The Tapti River originates from which mountain range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satpura Range**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tapti River originates from **Multai**, located in the **Satpura Range** of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• The Tapti River flows westward, one of the few rivers in peninsular India to do so, and drains into the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• It is approximately **724 km long**, making it one of the major rivers of central India.
 
• The Tapti River passes through three states: **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra,** and **Gujarat**.
 
• The river is known for supporting agricultural activities in its basin, which covers a total area of around **65,145 square kilometers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satpura Range:**

 
 
• The Satpura Range is a hill range in central India, stretching across Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
 
• The range is a part of the **Deccan Plateau** and is known for its rich biodiversity and dense forests.
 
• Prominent peaks in the Satpura Range include Dhupgarh (the highest point in Madhya Pradesh) and Pachmarhi.
 
• It is an important source of rivers such as the Tapti, Narmada, and Godavari.
 
 
 
• **Westward Flowing Rivers in India:**
 
 
• Most rivers in India flow eastward towards the Bay of Bengal; however, a few like the Tapti, Narmada, and Mahi flow westward.
 
• These rivers drain into the Arabian Sea, contributing significantly to the western coastal ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Arabian Sea Drainage System:**
 
 
• The Tapti River forms part of the Arabian Sea drainage system along with other westward flowing rivers.
 
• These rivers often carve narrow valleys and are important for irrigation and hydroelectric projects.
 
 
 
• **Multai:**
 
 
• Multai is a town in Madhya Pradesh known as the origin point of the Tapti River.
 
• The name "Tapti" is derived from the goddess Tapti, worshipped in Hindu mythology.

questions.question: According to the office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, a city with a population exceeding 10 million is classified as which type of urban settlement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mega City**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A city with a population exceeding 10 million is classified as a **Mega City** according to the office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
 
• Mega Cities are large urban areas with high population density and significant economic, social, and political influence.
 
• Examples of Mega Cities in India include **Delhi**, **Mumbai**, and **Kolkata**, as per recent census data.
 
• The term "Mega City" is used globally to categorize urban settlements with populations exceeding 10 million, aligning with United Nations standards.
 
• The classification helps in urban planning, resource allocation, and policy-making to address challenges like infrastructure, housing, and transportation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Settlements Classification**:

 
 
• Urban settlements are classified based on population size, density, and administrative importance.
 
• Categories include towns, cities, metropolitan cities, and mega cities.
 
• A Metropolitan City typically has a population between 1 million to 10 million.
 
 
 
• **Global Mega Cities**:
 
 
• Some of the world's largest Mega Cities include Tokyo, Shanghai, and São Paulo.
 
• These cities serve as hubs for finance, culture, and international trade.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Mega Cities**:
 
 
• Mega Cities often face issues such as overcrowding, pollution, inadequate infrastructure, and housing shortages.
 
• Governments implement policies to improve urban management and sustainability.
 
 
 
• **India's Census Data**:
 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years to collect demographic, social, and economic data.
 
• The classification of urban settlements is based on this data to ensure effective governance.

questions.question: The Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) was established in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1948**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) was established in **1948** by the Government of India.
 
• It was set up under the **Industrial Finance Corporation Act** to provide long-term financial support to industrial enterprises.
 
• IFCI was India's first development finance institution aimed at accelerating industrial growth in the country.
 
• Initially, it functioned as a statutory corporation before being converted into a company under the Companies Act in **1993**.
 
• IFCI plays a significant role in providing financial assistance for large-scale industrial projects and promoting industrial development across sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Development Finance Institutions (DFIs)**

 
 
• DFIs are financial institutions dedicated to providing long-term capital for industries and infrastructure projects.
 
• They aim to bridge the gap between the availability of funds and the financial needs of businesses that require large-scale investments.
 
• Examples include IFCI, IDBI, SIDBI, and NABARD.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of IFCI**
 
 
• From its inception in 1948, IFCI initially operated as a statutory body under the Industrial Finance Corporation Act.
 
• In 1993, it transitioned to a company structure under the Companies Act to enhance its operational flexibility.
 
• It has supported several key industries, including power, telecom, and manufacturing, through financial assistance.
 
 
 
• **Role in Industrial Growth**
 
 
• IFCI contributes to the industrialization of India by financing projects in sectors like energy, infrastructure, and technology.
 
• Its financial support aids in job creation, regional development, and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Current Status**
 
 
• IFCI is now a government-owned financial institution, with the majority stake held by the Government of India.
 
• It continues to play a vital role in financing industrial and infrastructure projects and remains relevant in the financial ecosystem of India.

questions.question: What is the Great Plain of Northern India popularly known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Plain of Northern India is popularly referred to as the **Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain** due to its formation by the three major river systems: the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra.
 
• This plain is one of the most fertile and extensive plains in the world, spanning approximately **7 lakh square kilometers**.
 
• It extends across northern and eastern India and also covers parts of Pakistan, Nepal, and Bangladesh.
 
• The plain is characterized by its **alluvial soil**, which is highly conducive to agriculture, making it a key food-producing region in India.
 
• It is divided into multiple sub-regions, including the Punjab Plains, Ganga Plains, and Brahmaputra Plains, based on the dominant river systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• The Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain is primarily composed of alluvial soil, which is formed by the deposition of sediments by rivers over time.
 
• This type of soil is rich in nutrients like phosphorous and potassium, making it ideal for cultivating crops such as rice, wheat, and sugarcane.
 
 
 
• **Division of the Plain:**
 
 
• The plain is divided into three major sections: the Western Plain (Punjab and Haryana), the Central Plain (Uttar Pradesh and Bihar), and the Eastern Plain (West Bengal and Assam).
 
• Each section has unique geographic and hydrological characteristics.
 
 
 
• **River Systems:**
 
 
• The plain is fed by three major river systems: the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra, along with their tributaries.
 
• These rivers play a crucial role in irrigation, transportation, and sustaining biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• Being highly fertile, the plain supports extensive agriculture, which is the backbone of the economy in this region.
 
• It is also a hub for industries such as textiles, sugar, and food processing due to the availability of raw materials and water resources.
 
 
 
• **Population Density:**
 
 
• The Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain is one of the most densely populated regions in the world due to its fertile land and availability of water.
 
• Major cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Patna, and Lucknow are located in this plain.

questions.question: Which island was renamed as Swaraj Dweep?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Havelock Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Havelock Island, part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, was renamed Swaraj Dweep in **December 2018** by the Government of India.
 
• The renaming was announced by PM Narendra Modi during the **celebration of the 75th anniversary of the hoisting of the Indian flag by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose** in Port Blair.
 
• The new name, Swaraj Dweep, pays tribute to Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, who referred to the Andaman Islands as the first Indian territory freed from British rule in 1943.
 
• Havelock Island is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the Andaman Islands, known for its pristine beaches like Radhanagar Beach and Elephant Beach.
 
• The renaming reflects India’s commitment to honor its historical heroes and their contributions to the country’s independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose and Andaman:**

 
 
• Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose hoisted the Indian flag on the Andaman Islands on **30 December 1943**, declaring it free from British rule.
 
• He named the Andaman and Nicobar Islands as Swaraj and Shaheed Dweep, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Renaming of Islands:**
 
 
• In addition to Havelock Island, two other islands were renamed: Ross Island became **Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep**, and Neil Island became **Shaheed Dweep**.
 
• The renaming initiative was part of an effort to align the islands' names with India’s freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Tourism at Swaraj Dweep:**
 
 
• Swaraj Dweep is famous for its crystal-clear waters, coral reefs, and adventure activities like snorkeling and scuba diving.
 
• Radhanagar Beach, located on the island, is often listed among Asia’s best beaches.
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:**
 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a union territory of India, comprising around 572 islands.
 
• They are located at the juncture of the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.
